title: MouseWithoutBorders does not pass keystrokes to remote machines when Prisma Browser is focused on primary machine
summary: Standalone Mouse Without Borders sends keyboard input to the focused Prisma Browser instead of the remote machine.

judgment.rationale: The scenario requires a discriminating comparison before the failing boundary can be established.
evidence: The reporter uses standalone Mouse Without Borders 2.2.1.0327 on Windows 11 25H2; mouse movement and clicks reach both secondary machines, but keyboard input goes to Prisma Browser on the primary.
The same setup works with Firefox, Chrome and Edge focused; Prisma Browser requires an employer-authorized account and may enforce enterprise security policy.

Inspected the PowerToys module source src/modules/MouseWithoutBorders/App/Class/InputHook.cs: it installs a low-level keyboard hook and routes input based on destination machine. This is not proof of the standalone build’s exact behavior.
judgment.recommended_action: Request the focused comparison and avoid claiming a cause or covering fix.

fix_assessment.rationale: A targeted correction or supported behavior investigation may be applicable after resolving the identified uncertainty.

proposed_fixes.title: Investigate managed browser keyboard forwarding
proposed_fixes.root_cause: A browser security policy or hook interaction may affect forwarding, but the reporter’s standalone-only result does not establish the cause or PowerToys-module behavior.
plan: First establish whether the same symptom occurs in the current PowerToys module as well as standalone MWB.
With authorized browser access, compare hook event delivery and destination routing for Prisma and a standard browser.
Coordinate with the browser and enterprise security team if policy controls the behavior; fix only a confirmed supported PowerToys defect without bypassing security.
Add focused regression coverage for any confirmed routing failure.
verification: With a permitted configuration, keyboard input reaches the selected remote machine in the confirmed supported case.
Local and remote input and enterprise protections remain intact.

confidence.rationale: The reported failure boundary and current behavior are not yet established.

comment.body: Thanks for the detailed comparison with Firefox, Chrome and Edge and for noting that this is standalone Mouse Without Borders. If your organization permits it, could you check whether the same issue occurs with the Mouse Without Borders module in the current PowerToys release, and share the PowerToys version and result? Use only non-sensitive test input and do not change or bypass the browser’s security policies.
